note.p: This seems to be a family whom Godwin is trying to assist to secure a pension either for the mother, or to have it transferred to the children after the mother's demise. The mother, Sophie Henriette Christiane, Baroness Walthausen swore an affadavit on the 24th of December 1813 in Hanover (Einbeir), following the death of her husband Charles Frederick William de Walthausen, a Captain in the 8th Battalion of the line of the King's German legion, in Sicily on the 9th of April 1813, affirming the validity of their marriage (in 1803)and her status as a widow. The Lieutenant General supported the request. It is unclear how Godwin knew them and became involved, but the close succession of visiting; the correspondence with Basil Montague (a lawyer), Godwin's writing for the family, were all clearly part of a campaign to secure acknowledgement of the Captain's service and his widow's rights. received by
